note: Designed structures — the Vision half of the map. These are what is PROPOSED for the land, never what stands on it (the county's own footprints are data/footprints.json and show only in Today mode). A structure moves through three states: 'site' is a reserved ground outline with nothing built on it, 'massing' extrudes that outline to a designed height, and 'model' places a real .glb through the three.js custom layer. Adding a building is a row here plus, for a model, a .glb under public/models or a full URL to one the engine serves — never a code change. A model with enter: true carries its own floors and walls (extras.walk) and the world lets you in; clears names the kinds of the standing record that come down for it.

structures.name: The Oak Leaf — massing
structures.note: The house proposed for the knoll, at real size: three leaves round the river-stone chimney that stands here today, the great room under the tall one, a loft over it, three suites cut into the south bank with the parking court below, the pool on the north side. The model's origin is the chimney; its main floor is the top of the knoll at 425.9 m. A massing, not a design: the shape at the right size on the right ground, to be walked round and argued with. Made by scripts/massing/oak-leaf.py in the engine repository, built at its deploy and served beside the world.
